subject: Critical Thinking
title: The Doctrine of Double Effect: Intent vs. Side Effect
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Doctrine of Double Effect: Intent vs. Side Effect.

hook.text: A doctor gives pain medication knowing it will shorten the patient's life. They intend to relieve pain, not to kill.

buildup.text: Doctrine of double effect: it may be permissible to cause harm as a side effect of achieving good, but not to cause.

discovery.text: Aquinas used it to distinguish intended harm from harm accepted as a side effect.

twist.text: This is why most people accept bombing a military target but reject using a human shield.

climax.text: Critics: the distinction between 'intended' & 'foreseen' is too thin.

punchline.text: What you intend matters. What you foresee also matters.

quiz.question: What does the doctrine of double effect distinguish between?
options: Harm caused as an intended means versus harm caused as a foreseen side effect

details.summary: The doctrine of double effect holds that it can be permissible to cause harm as an unintended side effect of a good action, but impermissible to cause the same harm intentionally. Intent, not outcome, makes the moral difference.
details.whyItMatters: This principle shapes medical ethics, military rules of engagement, and legal standards for negligence versus murder.
takeaways: Intended harm is morally different from foreseen but unintended harm
The action itself must be morally neutral or good
The good effect must not be achieved through the bad effect

faq.question: How does double effect apply in medical decisions?
faq.answer: A doctor may give pain medication that shortens life if the intent is pain relief, not death. The harmful side effect is permissible because it is not the means to the good outcome.

faq.question: What are the main conditions for double effect to apply?
faq.answer: The action must be good or neutral, the bad effect must not be intended, the good effect must not depend on the bad one, and the good must be proportionate to the harm.
